type: Offline post-hoc finite coding discovery, not independent model trials
question: Can compact exact-priced quantizers on larger groups improve C74 at common finite lengths?
starts: C69 three-block book times the C72 constant-pair responses
rng: xorshift32, 0x9e3779b9 + seed*7919, distinct initial unsigned response words
direction: Float ECVQ assignments/centroids only select a proposal; freeze final word order and positive integer proposal counts
exact_encoder: Minimize 2^(b*L(x,w))/q_w^a at price a/b, ties by public book order
fallback: Public response with largest proposal weight, ties by first book index; exact-price minimization guarantees no larger group loss for any source
arithmetic_counts: Actual exact-rule source occupancies, which may differ from proposal counts; never transmit an instance histogram
conditional_extension: If five blocks do not improve the C74 finite bound at k=12288, run group six at price 2/5 from the C69 component product and a random 16384-word book. Preserve all first-stage outcomes.
tail: Public remaining r<g blocks each use a charged two-bit nearest scalar response from [0,1,14,15]
runtime_scope: Bounded group/cardinality/update searches and separately measured local actors; no portable latency guarantee
numeric_contract: Exact integer price comparisons, complete uniform-group source occupancy/loss grading and outward rational entropy/weighted overflow bounds
information_contract: Uniform iid four-bit blocks; parent before R/O, exactly 2*k bits including the full-group fallback flag and tail labels; child one bit before J; final only Z/R/O/J; all designs before X
